units.function: Route and database-oriented tests for cost/finance summaries, budget mutation authority, unpriced usage, recursive issue/run attribution and integer-overflow-resistant aggregates.
units.dependencyDirection: Vitest -> real cost routes with mocked services plus cost/finance services with embedded PostgreSQL when available; route actors/services and persistence tests are separated, so no test spans authorization through durable budget/evidence state.
units.keyDataModels: CostEvent provider/biller/billingType/costStatus/model/tokens/cents/time, FinanceEvent kind/currency/direction/estimated, company/Agent budgets and policies, issue tree, heartbeat Run duration and activity-based attribution.
units.lifecycle: Connector/runtime reports usage/cost -> event is stored and spend may update -> operators query company/provider/Agent/project/issue summaries -> human board users change budget/policy -> runtime may later enforce incidents and cancellation outside this suite.
units.testAssessment: Approved unsandboxed Vitest passed 12 route/parser tests while 5 embedded-Postgres tests remained skipped; sandboxed results were 5 passed, 7 Supertest-listen failures and 5 skipped. Intended database coverage is thoughtful—unpriced usage, >int32 sums, recursive costs/runtime—but is not executable evidence in this environment. End-to-end budget enforcement, transactional mutation and ingestion idempotency are absent.
units.designRationale: Separate provider usage from billable spend, preserve unpriced subscription work, support operational cost rollups by organizational/work hierarchy and keep budget changes human-board-only.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs trustworthy multi-provider/model/data/tool cost and usage accounting for Agent Boss decisions, data-export governance, managed/self-hosted deployment and FDE pilots measuring real human-plus-Agent delivery economics.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT the append-only typed event shape, unpriced-versus-zero distinction, provider/biller separation, recursive work attribution and wide numeric aggregation. Add provider event idempotency, price/rate-card snapshot and later reconciliation, currency-safe ledgers, usage and monetary policies, explicit overhead allocation, immutable responsibility/evidence links and one transactional/versioned budget command with an outbox for runtime enforcement.
units.responsibilityConflict: Cost events are attributed to Agent/project/issue but not to requester, accountable human, data/tool authority, approval or result evidence. Budget mutation updates three observable concerns through separate mocked calls; the suite cannot prove the human decision, policy state, legacy field and audit evidence remain atomic.

2026-08-19 approved unsandboxed focused Vitest: 12 passed, 5 embedded-Postgres tests skipped
units.securityFindings: HIGH budget-integrity gap: Agent field update, policy upsert and activity evidence are separate mocked calls with no transaction, optimistic version, idempotency or rollback test. HIGH accounting-integrity gap: no provider event identity/deduplication, signed source, rate-card version or reconciliation prevents duplicate/fabricated/stale costs. HIGH currency risk: finance summaries are tested only with USD even though events carry currency; cross-currency arithmetic is not guarded here. MEDIUM visibility risk: skill-test harness costs/runs are excluded from issue-tree rollups and could hide delivery overhead unless separately disclosed. MEDIUM resource/precision gaps include unconstrained date windows, weak limit boundaries, JavaScript safe-integer/rounding limits and live orphan Run duration. Actual DB tests were skipped, weakening persistence evidence.
